_note: Common mistakes (/grammatik/typische-fehler): English words learners mix up. Each pair has two sides (a, b: the word, its part of speech or a note, an example with <b>), `why` the difference in one sentence, `tr` its translation into the help languages (empty: English is the only help language for now, the page shows nothing then), `check` a gap to try (`answer` = a or b; `options` when the words on the buttons are not the bare a/b words). `regel` per group is the folding rule (*…* = example, **…** = bold), `regelTr` its translation (empty, as `tr`), `comic` the comic at the top (MascotComic). `wrong: true` on b = this is not correct English. Meaning traps (false friends, kitchen/chicken) are on /wissen/wortfallen, not here. The part-of-speech cards on /grammatik/wortarten point to a pair here through `fehler`. British English; idioms-mistakes run (2026-10-30), not yet reviewed.

left.name: regi
left.say: No apostrophe there! {its} tail = the dog's tail.

right.name: quaki
right.say: Oh – so the apostrophe means a missing letter!

left.name: hamsti
left.say: Can you say {it is}? Then write {it's}!

regel: You can't hear the difference – you only see it. Ask yourself: **what kind of word** is it?
An apostrophe often shows a missing letter: *it's = it is*, *you're = you are*, *who's = who is*.
Can you say *it is* or *you are* instead? Then write the short form with an apostrophe. If not, write *its*, *your*, *whose*.
groups.title: Sounds the same, spelt differently
groups.lead: You can't hear the difference. In writing you see it at once.

b.pos: short form: it is / it has

pairs.why: it's = it is or it has. its (no apostrophe) = belonging to it.

check.gap: The company changed ___ name last year.

pairs.why: you're = you are. your = belonging to you.

check.gap: Thank you, ___ very kind.

a.pos: place, or there is / there are

pairs.why: their = belonging to them. there = a place, or there is / there are.

check.gap: The children are playing with ___ dog.

pairs.why: too means also, or more than is good. In every other case it is to.

check.gap: You're going to the party? I'd like to come ___!

b.pos: short form: who is / who has

pairs.why: who's = who is or who has. whose asks who something belongs to.

check.gap: ___ phone is ringing?

pairs.why: You hear with your ear – and hear has ear in it. here = in this place.

check.gap: I've lived ___ in Leeds since 2020.

a.ex: I want to buy a new phone.

pairs.why: buy = pay money for something. by = how you travel, or next to something.

check.gap: We travelled to Glasgow ___ train.

regel: Always a capital letter: **I**, names, days, months, countries, languages and nationalities: *Monday, June, France, English, Polish*.
A small letter: the seasons and most other words: *spring, summer, school, teacher*.
The first word of a sentence always starts with a capital letter.
groups.title: Capital letter or not?
groups.lead: In English, some words need a capital letter in the middle of a sentence – and some don't.

b.ex: Never a small i on its own.

pairs.why: The word I is always a capital letter, also in the middle of a sentence.

check.gap: On Sundays ___ visit my grandmother.

b.ex: Languages always need a capital letter.

pairs.why: Languages and nationalities start with a capital letter: English, French, Polish.

check.gap: My ___ teacher is from Wales.

pairs.why: Days and months start with a capital letter: Monday, July.

check.gap: The meeting is on ___ morning.

pairs.why: The seasons have a small letter: spring, summer, autumn, winter.

check.gap: We always go to the beach in the ___.

pairs.why: When you talk to her, Mum works like a name: capital. After my, your or his it is a small letter.

check.gap: Thanks for dinner, ___!

regel: These words are close in sound or spelling, but they are **different words**.
Learn each one with an example: *bigger than*, *and then*, *lose your keys*, *loose jeans*.
Not sure? Say it aloud: *quiet* has two syllables (qui-et), *quite* has one.
groups.title: Sounds almost the same
groups.lead: Two words, one small difference – in the sound, the spelling or both.

a.ex: We had dinner and then went for a walk.

pairs.why: than compares two things (bigger than). then is about time (and then).

check.gap: My flat is smaller ___ yours.

pairs.why: lose /luːz/ is a verb. loose /luːs/ is an adjective: not tight.

check.gap: I always ___ my umbrella on the train.

pairs.why: quiet (qui-et, two syllables) = not loud. quite (one syllable) = fairly.

check.gap: Please be ___, the baby is asleep.

b.ex: I advise you to see a doctor.

pairs.why: advice with c is the noun, advise with s is the verb. British English does the same with practice (noun) and practise (verb).

check.gap: Thanks for your ___ – it really helped.

pairs.why: accept = say yes to something. except = but not.

check.gap: The shop is open every day ___ Sunday.

pairs.why: live (short i) = have your home somewhere. leave (long ee) = go away.

check.gap: What time do you ___ the office?

a.pos: noun: sweet food after a meal

pairs.why: dessert has two s – because you always want a second one!

check.gap: What would you like for ___? – Chocolate cake, please!

pairs.why: feel → felt. fall → fell.

check.gap: He slipped on the ice and ___.

a.ex: Would you like a cup of tea?

pairs.why: off (two f) is the opposite of on. of joins two nouns: a cup of tea.

check.gap: Please switch ___ your phone in the cinema.

regel: Don't translate fixed expressions word for word from your first language.
Learn them as whole sentences: *I'm cold. I'm 20. I agree. You're right.*
groups.title: Fixed expressions
groups.lead: Translated word for word it sounds right – but it isn't English.

b.ex: Translated from French or Spanish (j'ai froid, tengo frío).

pairs.why: Feelings like cold, hot, hungry and thirsty go with be: I'm cold. (I have a cold means you are ill.)

check.gap: Can you close the window, please? ___

b.ex: Translated from Spanish, French or Italian.

pairs.why: Say your age with be: I'm 20, or I'm 20 years old.

check.gap: How old is your son? – ___

pairs.why: agree is a verb, like like or know: I agree, I don't agree.

check.gap: That's a great idea. ___

b.ex: Translated from German or Spanish (ein Foto machen, hacer una foto).

pairs.why: In English you take a photo.

check.gap: Excuse me, could you ___ a photo of us?

b.ex: Translated from German, French or Polish (du hast recht, tu as raison).

pairs.why: Use be: you're right, I was wrong.

check.gap: It's getting late. – Yes, ___

a.pos: right: for + a length of time

b.ex: since needs a point in time: since 2022, since Monday.

pairs.why: for + a length of time (three years). since + a point in time (2022, Monday).

check.gap: She has worked here ___ two months.

a.ex: I need some information about the course.

b.ex: information has no plural and no a/an.

pairs.why: information, advice, news and furniture are uncountable: no -s, no a/an.

check.gap: Could you send me some ___ about the flat?

b.ex: explain needs to before the person.

pairs.why: You explain something to someone: Can you explain it to me?

check.gap: Can you ___ how this machine works?

regel: **behind** + a noun or pronoun: *behind the house, behind me*.
**at the back / at the front** = in the back or front part of something: *at the back of the bus*.
**in front of** = just before something; **opposite** = on the other side, facing it: *opposite the bank*.
groups.title: behind, at the back, opposite
groups.lead: Where is it? Small words, big difference.

a.ex: Let's sit at the back of the bus.

pairs.why: behind = outside, after something. at the back = the back part inside it: at the back of the cinema.

check.gap: The car park is ___ the supermarket.

a.ex: There's a bus stop in front of the school.

b.ex: The driver sits at the front of the bus.

pairs.why: in front of = outside, before it. at the front = the front part inside it.

check.gap: I want to sit ___ in class so I can see the board.

a.pos: on the other side, facing it

b.ex: The taxi stopped in front of our house.

pairs.why: opposite = across the road or room, facing it. in front of = directly before it, on the same side.

check.gap: The café is ___ the park, on the other side of the road.
